This is apples-to-apples for the major bottlenecks, with some error for the "cold" parts. Any other ideas? First one is beyond my skills, but for synthetic part I’ll try to add counters early next week and post the numbers here Then we can try synthetic benchmarks in both EVM and native code My concern is that a control flow will be very non-trivial and may add a good penalty Sounds good.

excerpts.content: For sanity-checking eip-2929, this gist can be used: https://gist.github.com/holiman/8f54f24008b57d303c92f24732a14943 . excerpts.content:
<@!682078300234973185> For "apples to apples" 1962 codebase with turbo boost off (this is important) gives the following for BLS12-381 without subgroup checks (just the pairing) for 2 and 4 pairs
```
test bench::bls12_381_engine::bench_bls12_engine_pair_2                                 ... bench:   3,132,650 ns/iter (+/- 13,014)
test bench::bls12_381_engine::bench_bls12_engine_pair_4                                 ... bench:   4,331,603 ns/iter (+/- 64,513)
```

Turbo boost is roughly -30% from the numbers cause benchmark is short, CPU bound and CPU frequency flies from 2.9 to 4+ GHz
